messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT - High egress error rate for eu-west-3 private subnets (service: inference-egress). Investigate. https://pd.example/INC-4532 :rotating_light:

alice: seeing lots of 502s from customers in EU, alerts started ~08:12 UTC. Routing & NAT look suspect. paging net oncall - @carla-netops can you take?

carla-netops: I’m on it. Taking bridge. Can someone confirm which AZs impacted?

ben-sre: I have telemetry from infra: az3 private subnets show spike in TCP resets and SYN retries. az1/az2 look fine.

alice: confirmed from logs: most errors originate from 10.20.48.0/22 (az3-private-1).

dave-support: customer impact: a handful of enterprise customers report downstream HTTP timeouts for webhooks. Support escalation open -> CS case 8902.

carla-netops: checking route tables now. running: 
```bash
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-az3-private-1" --query 'RouteTables[*].{ID:RouteTableId,Routes:Routes}'
```

carla-netops: route table looks correct, default route -> nat-instance-az3 (legacy NAT instance), not NAT Gateway. Hmm.

eve-eng: we still have a couple legacy NAT instances for cost reasons in az3; were they part of yesterday's infra rollout?

deploy-bot: terraform apply completed by @frank at 07:58 UTC to update autoscale policy for nat-asg-eu-west-3. No explicit SG edits recorded in the plan, but a separate automation changed security groups at 08:05 UTC (sg-sync job).

carla-netops: SSHing to nat instance (10.0.128.45) to check conntrack / iptables.

carla-netops: ran these: 
```bash
ssh ubuntu@10.0.128.45 'sudo conntrack -S | head -n 40'
# output: entries: 524288, conntrack table full?
sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v
# MASQUERADE rules present
```

carla-netops: conntrack table at or near limit, lots of CLOSE_WAIT and TIME_WAIT. I suspect ephemeral port restrictions from SG change caused source ports to be reused more aggressively.

ben-sre: can you paste recent SG changes? I’ll pull audit logs.

carla-netops: checked CloudTrail: sg-0a1b2c3d had an update at 08:05 UTC from sg-sync-bot: inbound rule tightened to allow only ephemeral ports 1024-32768? That seems wrong for nat-instance since it handles ephemeral mappings dynamically.

alice: summary: automation tightened SG on NAT instances -> blocked higher ephemeral ranges -> connections half-succeed, half-stall -> conntrack entries accumulate -> table fills -> new connections reset.

dave-support: CS: customers see intermittent 502s and timeouts between 08:12-08:35 UTC. Impact window matches.

ben-sre: mitigation plan: 1) widen SG back to original ephemeral range 1024-65535 2) clear conntrack on nat instance 3) scale up nat-asg temporarily 4) monitor. Who can revert SG?

carla-netops: I can revert. Performing revert now and will keep you updated.

carla-netops: Reverted sg-0a1b2c3d to previous rules (allowing 1024-65535 outbound). CloudTrail event id: abc123.

carla-netops: flushing conntrack on nat instance: 
```bash
ssh ubuntu@10.0.128.45 'sudo conntrack -F'
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2621440
```

carla-netops: scaling nat-asg-eu-west-3 +2 instances to spread load: 
```bash
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name nat-asg-eu-west-3 --desired-capacity 4
```

ben-sre: seeing immediate drop in reset rates and successful flows ramping. p95 request latency back to baseline in az3.

alice: monitoring logs for 10 minutes to confirm.

eve-eng: also pushed a temporary route fallback policy to route new sessions to nat-gateway-standby in az2 for cross-AZ resilience (policy window 30m). Command: 
```bash
# update routing association (canary)
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --instance-id NAT-GW-STANDBY
```

dave-support: notifying affected customers: initial message sent, will update in 30m if stable.

ben-sre: can everyone check checks: 
- nat conntrack freed (yes)
- SG reverted (yes)
- ASG scaled (yes)
- fallback routing in place (yes)

alice: marking incident severity reduced to SEV2 (no longer wide outage, limited customer impact).

deploy-bot: sg-sync job paused for eu-west-3 by @carla-netops at 08:46 UTC to prevent flapping.

carla-netops: next steps: 1) audit sg-sync rules to ensure NAT instances are excluded from ephemeral port tightening 2) schedule removal/replace legacy NAT instances with managed NAT Gateway in eu-west-3 3) add conntrack headroom alert and automated scaling.

eve-eng: I’ll raise a PR to replace nat-asg with nat-gw + plan to migrate next week, will include rollout playbook.

dave-support: CS update: two enterprise customers reported brief retries; no data loss. Case notes updated.

alice: closing the active paging loop; hand off to postmortem owner @ben-sre. Please capture timeline and action items. :thumbsup:

ben-sre: acknowledged. I’ll own postmortem and follow up with root cause (sg-sync policy + legacy NAT pattern) and remediation timeline.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-4532 transitioned to "resolved" by ben-sre at 08:53 UTC.

carla-netops: final checks: p50/p95 latency stable across az3, conntrack counts normal. Leaving ASG at desired=4 for 10m then scale back.

alice: thanks everyone — incident thread archived, postmortem due in 48h.

deploy-bot: automated ticket created: PM-3287 (Migrate eu-west-3 to NAT Gateway), SRE-789 (Add conntrack headroom alert), OPS-456 (Exclude NAT instances from sg-sync).
